text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz has consulted with President Demirel about who should be included in the cabinet of Yilmaz's planned coalition.
- The Turkish economy needs drastic measures from the new government.
- The Yilmaz government will give priority to the economy and secularist education.
- Demirel will approve the Yilmaz government today.
- Italian giant Benetton to buy cotton from southeast Turkeuy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party is crumbling away.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is channeling trillions of lira of government money to town councils controlled by his Islam-based Welfare Party in his last days in power.
- State-owned Ziraat Bankasi searching for funding abroad.
- The Istanbul stock exchange is indexed to political events in Ankara.
